$comment: The source of sf-code-input's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/code-input (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

length.summary: How many characters the code has, 1 to 12; one cell each.

default-value.summary: The code a form reset returns to; the field starts with it when there is no value.

name.summary: The form name of the native input, which is the form value.

mode.summary: numeric: digits, a digit keyboard; alphanumeric: Latin letters and digits. Anything else typed or pasted is left out; the native pattern asks for exactly length characters of the mode.

size.summary: A step of the form-field ladder, as sf-input's: the cells and their text.

appearance.summary: bordered: cells divided by a border; filled: cells on a tonal fill, which become bordered while the code has focus.

label.summary: The visible label; it names the group and the field.

hint.summary: Text under the cells: how many characters, where the code comes from.

required.summary: The form asks for a whole code.

invalid.summary: The code was refused: cells and hint in the error colour, aria-invalid on the field. The host sets and clears it.

error-message.summary: Shown in place of the hint while invalid, and the field's aria-errormessage.

mask.summary: Each character shows as a dot; the field is a password field, so a screen reader does not read the code out.

value.summary: The code. Written as an attribute it is controlled: the attribute follows what the person types. Kept to the mode and the length.

input.summary: The code changed while typing, pasting or by autofill; the native event bubbles from the inner input, which is its target, with the value already kept to the mode and the length. It carries no detail.

change.summary: The code was committed: the field lost focus with a code other than the one it had when it took focus. Sent once from the inner input. It carries no detail.

completed.summary: The fact completed (standard 1.3.8 §8): every cell holds a character, after an edit the person made; once for each whole code, after its input event. The element never submits the form.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-code-input for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.note: stays a host attribute, read by the base (§3.1, §4.8); no shim

rows.summary: Legacy name of sf-code-input-completed, sent after it with the same detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json, standard 1.3.8 §16.20).

rows.note: error is a dated alias of invalid; the shim maps the attribute and the property
rows.summary: Legacy name for invalid, still honoured.

x-summary: A one-time code -- from a message, an authenticator, an email -- as a form field with its own value, paste and errors, drawn as the class verification: one native input holds the code (autocomplete one-time-code, so autofill and WebOTP fill it whole) and the cells picture it. Typing fills the next cell, Backspace steps back and clears, a pasted code fills every cell, and each cell is announced by its place.
x-renamed: settings.aria-label: a host attribute, read by the base, never a setting (§3.1)
settings.length: type string with the numeral default "6" → number (§16 item 29)
x-decisions: alias-conflict: the fact is `completed` (sf-code-input-completed), as vocabulary 1.1.5 §9 writes it; the old sf-code-input:complete is its dated same-detail alias. The alias table's earlier sf-code-input-complete was never shipped, so it gets no row.
version 1.1.0: renamed members behind dated aliases (completed, invalid) are a minor (§4.10).

key-effects: ArrowLeft focus:prev, ArrowRight focus:next, Home to:first, End to:last (the cells), Backspace focus:prev (it clears the cell before the caret and steps back), Tab reach; Delete stays the text box's own editing key, with no effect of the closed list; probe.json drives every declared key (gate 16).
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles one (a copy nothing draws would drift).
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (three of six digits) plus a complete code, alphanumeric, masked, four cells, filled, invalid, disabled and size 2.
css-variables: the seven --sf-verification-* variables of the class sheet sf-code-input draws with, plus --sf-verification-invalid-border-color for the invalid state (§6).
error -> invalid (§17.2): a dated setting alias.
form.validity: value-missing and pattern-mismatch (an incomplete code) from the input, and custom-error (§17.2).
form: the host submits the code through ElementInternals; the input carries no name (§17.1 item 6).
ids: the label, position line and message ids come from the field's instance path (field.base), not the module counter it had (§7.1.1, simai/ui-source#41).
words: digit, character and group are lang runtime words read with sfWord; CODE_INPUT_TEXT stays in code.mjs for its unit tests only.

version 1.1.2: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

$comment: sf-code-input loads on demand like any other Smart element. It draws the
class verification's markup, so the class verification is what it draws
with: its sheet (and its runtime, which leaves the element's field alone),
and the sr-only utility for the line that says which cell the caret is in.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-code-input for a one-time code a person types or pastes -- from a text message, an authenticator app, an email -- as a field of a native form.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not use it for a PIN or password the person chooses: that is sf-input with input-type password
Do not submit the form or check the code from the complete event alone: the host checks it
Do not restyle its cells: they are the class verification's, set its public variables
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <sf-code-input label="Код из сообщения" name="code" hint="Мы отправили шесть цифр на +7 900 000-00-00"></sf-code-input>

accessibility.focus: The group (role group) and the one native input are named by the label, or by aria-label without one. The input is described by a polite line that says the caret's cell -- «цифра 3 из 6», «digit 3 of 6», «символ» or «character» for an alphanumeric code -- in the page's language, said again each time the caret changes cell; then by the hint or the error message. Typing fills the caret's cell and moves on, Backspace clears the cell before the caret and steps back, the arrows, Home and End move between the cells, a click puts the caret in the cell clicked. The cells are aria-hidden; the characters run left to right in a right-to-left page too.

sf-code-input:complete.summary: Legacy name of sf-code-input-completed, sent after it with the same detail until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json, standard 1.3.8 §16.20).

getInputElement.summary: Returns the inner native input, or null before render.

aria-label.description: The name of the group and the field when there is no visible label.
